newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan, US, UK plan conference on commodities trade.
newsitem.headline: Japan, US, UK plan conference on commodities trade.

text.p: Commodity trade regulators from the United States, Britain and Japan plan to hold an international conference on market surveillance in late November or early December, a Trade Ministry official said on Tuesday.

They will seek ways to cooperate on greater exchanges of information and measures to prevent market manipulation in the aftermath of Sumitomo Corp's huge trading losses in worldwide copper markets, the official said.
Sumitomo announced on June 13 that it had lost an estimated $1.8 billion in unauthorised copper trades over a decade, mainly by its former star trader Yasuo Hamanaka.
Officials of the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission, Britain's Securities and Investments Board and Japan's Trade and Agriculture ministries are to attend the meeting, the official said.
It has not been decided yet where the meeting will be held.
"We'll have detailed discussions on commodity market surveillance following the Sumitomo copper scandal. Regulators from other countries are welcome to attend the meeting," the official said.
